2027-03-30.title: Tuesday of Hevoro week · Easter Tuesday
readings: Christ our paschal lamb has been sacrificed; let us celebrate the festival
A lamp is put on the lampstand; the measure you give
2027-03-30.alt: Hevoro week, the first week of the season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection). Hevoro means white: the week is kept as one great day of Easter joy.
2027-03-30.verse: For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
theo: Three days ago the Church kept Pesaha; today St Paul tells us what Pesaha now means. “For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed. Therefore, let us celebrate the festival, not with the old yeast, the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.” Paul is writing to Corinth about a scandal the community had tolerated, and he uses the image every Jewish family knew: before Passover the house is searched and every bit of leaven is cleared out, because “a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.” The Passover lamb was sacrificed so that Israel might pass from slavery to freedom; Christ, the true Lamb, was sacrificed on the Cross so that we might pass from death to life. St John Chrysostom, commenting on these verses, said that for the Christian the whole of life is a festival, because the Lamb has been offered for us (in substance). We keep that festival above all at the altar, where the Lamb who was sacrificed and is now risen gives himself to us, truly present, Body and Blood, soul and divinity. Many St Thomas Christian homes ate unleavened Pesaha bread last Thursday; Paul asks us to become unleavened bread ourselves, people of sincerity and truth.

The Gospel continues the Easter light. “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed, and not on the lampstand? For there is nothing hidden, except to be disclosed; nor is anything secret, except to come to light.” On Good Friday the light of the world was hidden in the tomb; on Qyomtho it was set on the lampstand for all to see. No stone could keep it under the bed. Now the risen Lord puts his light in us, and he does not want it hidden by fear or by shame. Then Jesus adds a warning that is also a promise: “Pay attention to what you hear; the measure you give will be the measure you get, and still more will be given you.” Easter faith grows when it is given away. The one who shares the joy of the Resurrection receives more of it; the one who keeps it under the bed may find even what he has slipping away.

Hevoro week is a good time to clear out old yeast. Paul names it: malice and evil. In a family it may be an old resentment, a habit of sarcasm, a lie that has never been put right. Easter is the moment to throw it out, as a household clears the leaven before the feast. Practically: go to the Holy Qurbono today if you can, and receive the Lamb with a clean heart; this evening, let each person at home say one thing he or she is sorry for and one thing he or she is thankful for; and then set your Easter light on the lampstand by one visible act of goodness tomorrow, at work, in school or in the neighbourhood. Keep greeting one another with the Easter greeting all this week.

2027-03-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, our paschal Lamb, you were sacrificed for us and you are risen. Clear out of our hearts the old yeast of malice and evil, and make us unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. You give yourself to us at your altar; make our whole life a festival of thanksgiving. Let the light you have kindled in us shine on the lampstand, so that others may see it and come to you. Amen.
altar: On the altar the paschal Lamb, sacrificed once and now risen, gives himself to us truly; this is the festival Paul calls us to keep.

quick: Christ our paschal lamb has been sacrificed; let us keep the feast with sincerity and truth.
A little yeast leavens the whole batch: clear out the old yeast of malice.
A lamp is put on the lampstand; the measure you give will be the measure you get.
2027-03-30.action: Give up one resentment today as your Easter offering.
2027-03-30.question: Is my Easter light on the lampstand, or under the bed?

family.explain: Jesus asks: would you light a lamp and then hide it under your bed? Of course not! You put it up high so that everyone can see. Jesus is risen, and he has put his light in our hearts. We should not hide it. We let it shine by being kind, honest and joyful.
family.intention: We pray that our family may shine with Jesus' Easter light.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can let Jesus' light shine tomorrow?”

illus: A family in Pathanamthitta used to make their Pesaha bread from a recipe written in a grandmother's hand. One year the mother found, folded inside the recipe card, a second note in the same hand: before you make this bread, make peace with anyone you are angry with; the bread will taste better. The family laughed, then went quiet. That Easter week the mother finally rang her brother, to whom she had not spoken in three years over a land dispute. They did not settle the land that day. But he came to their house on New Sunday, and the children met their cousins for the first time.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, our paschal Lamb, we gather in your light. Clear our hearts and make us new. Amen.
share: Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch (1 Corinthians 5:7). What old yeast do I need to clear out?
Let us celebrate the festival... with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5:8). Is my life sincere and truthful?
Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket? (Mark 4:21). Where am I hiding my faith?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, let your light shine in us.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the festival of Easter with sincerity and truth.
For families divided by old quarrels, that this Easter may bring reconciliation.
For all who will receive the Holy Qurbono this week, that they may receive the Lamb with clean hearts.
For those who are ashamed of their faith, that they may set their light on the lampstand.
For the newly baptized, that their Easter light may never be hidden.
pm.close: Father, you gave us your Son as our paschal Lamb and raised him in glory. Make us a new batch, free of malice, and let the light of his Resurrection shine through us for all to see. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today St Paul says: for our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed. Therefore, let us celebrate the festival (1 Corinthians 5:7–8). Easter is the true Pesaha. The Lamb was sacrificed on the Cross, and he is alive.

Before Passover, Jewish families clear every bit of leaven from the house. Paul says: clean out the old yeast, the yeast of malice and evil. A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough (1 Corinthians 5:6). One unforgiven hurt can sour a whole family.

Jesus asks: is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed? (Mark 4:21). The tomb could not hide the Light. Now he has lit his light in us. We are not to hide it out of fear or shame.

And the measure you give will be the measure you get (Mark 4:24). Easter joy grows when it is shared. Let us receive the Lamb at the Holy Qurbono with clean hearts, give up one resentment, and let our light shine. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus said: nobody lights a lamp and puts it under the bed. A lamp is for shining! Jesus has put his light in your heart. You can let it shine today by being kind to someone, by telling the truth, and by saying with a big smile: Christ is risen!

concl: Christ our Passover has been sacrificed and is risen; the whole Christian life is his festival.
Clear out the old yeast, and let the Easter light shine.
